definitions.explanation: The place on a riverbank or shore where a ferry boat takes on and lets off passengers. Common in descriptions of pre-modern travel, before bridges were built.

examples.english: To wait for the boat at the ferry landing.
Long ago there was a ferry crossing on this river.

examples.japanese: ⟦{橋|はし}→橋：02163_hashi⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦できる→できる：00557_dekiru⟧⟦{前|まえ}→前：02255_mae⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧、⟦{村|むら}→村：02261_mura⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{人|ひと}→人：00476_hito⟧たち⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧{渡|わた}し{場|ば}⟦から→から：00504_kara⟧⟦{舟|ふね}→舟：23868_fune⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{乗|の}って→乗る：00511_noru⟧⟦{対岸|たいがん}→対岸：17100_taigan⟧⟦へ→へ：02473_he⟧⟦{渡|わた}っていた→渡る：02441_wataru⟧。
examples.english: Before the bridge was built, the villagers boarded boats at the ferry landing and crossed to the far bank.

notes:
From ⟦{渡|わた}す→渡す：02442_watasu⟧ (to carry across) + ⟦{場|ば}→場：03699_ba⟧ (place). Many Japanese place names preserve old crossings, and the word appears frequently in historical fiction and local history.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {渡|わた}し{場|ば}⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{着|つ}く→着く：00680_tsuku⟧: to reach the ferry landing
- {渡|わた}し{場|ば}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{跡|あと}→跡：02174_ato⟧: the site of a former ferry crossing
- {渡|わた}し{船|ぶね}: a ferry boat

SIMILAR WORDS:
- ⟦{船着|ふなつ}き{場|ば}→船着き場：21296_funatsukiba⟧: boat landing, dock — any place boats tie up, not necessarily a crossing
- ⟦{港|みなと}→港：01512_minato⟧: harbor, port — much larger, for shipping rather than a short crossing
